b: PARIS — UFI, The Global Association of the Exhibition Industry, held its 93rd Global Congress in the Kingdom of Bahrain on Nov. 2-5, 2026.

Hosted by Exhibition World Bahrain (EWB) and Bahrain Tourism & Exhibitions Authority (BTEA), the event brought together a wealth of global participants to explore the opportunities and challenges shaping the future of the events industry.

Trade Show Executive’s (TSE) Young Professionals Corner sat down with Chris Skeith, OBE, UFI’s CEO & Managing Director, to learn about this momentous event and how YPs can get involved and prepare for success in 2027.
In 2026, the event’s theme was “Stronger Connections, Smarter Futures.”
ANDREW: What were some major themes at the 93rd UFI Global Congress?

CHRIS: Our theme this year was “Stronger Connections, Smarter Futures.” Across the main stage, the discussion centered on how exhibitions can navigate uncertainty, embrace innovation and deliver greater value.
A panel of senior leaders from across the Gulf Cooperation Council highlighted the importance of collaboration, adaptability and rebuilding confidence to support future growth.
In his keynote, Lord Stephen A. Carter of Informa spoke about the enduring power of face-to-face relationships and the role of accurate data in creating more personalized live experiences.
Closing keynote speaker Hugh Jones of RX explored the importance of delivering meaningful experiences in an increasingly digital world.
ANDREW: How did it benefit UFI members and the industry as a whole?
CHRIS: More than ever, it proved the value of meeting face-to-face.
In times of change, connecting people matters, and it makes a real difference.

The geopolitical landscape is high on our members’ radar: In our Global Exhibition Barometer, concluded in June 2026, geopolitical challenges ranked as the second most pressing business issue globally, and was a top concern in the Middle East & Africa.
Delivering an event for our community in the region was a strong show of solidarity, and a reminder of the value our events bring.
For EWB and BTEA, it was an opportunity to showcase the world-class facilities, connections and talent they offer, and they did so to great effect.
ANDREW: How was its location chosen and how did it enhance the show?
CHRIS: The location was chosen through a lengthy RFP process.
For EWB and BTEA, it was an opportunity to showcase the world-class facilities, connections and talent they offer, and they did so to great effect.
Delegate experience and feedback have been very strong.
ANDREW: What were some highlights this year?
CHRIS: The keynotes from industry leaders stood out, sharing how they approach the sector and how the sector is approaching the market.

The welcome and hospitality were on another level, with great attention to detail, and every delegate made to feel valued and welcome. And then there was the region itself: so well connected, with such a rich history and of course the people who looked after us.

ANDREW: What was new at the Global Congress this year?
CHRIS: We are always evolving the format of the event. This year, our Insight Series drew on the experiences of three UFI Awards 2026 winners: itemdrop, Informa Markets ASEAN and Better Stands.

Working in newsroom teams, delegates created their own front pages for 2030, imagining what our industry might look like and what could change. Follow-up webinars will ensure the best practice we rewarded is shared more widely than just at the event.

The Congress also marked a change in leadership. Wolfram Diener, CEO of Messe Düsseldorf, became UFI President for 2026-2027, succeeding Panittha Buri, and our new Board of Directors for 2026-2029 and Executive Committee began their mandates.

We were also delighted to sign a multi-year agreement with EWB, which joined UFI as a Diamond Sponsor, our highest tier of sponsorship. The partnership builds on the legacy of their hosting of the Congress and reflects a shared commitment to the growth of the global exhibition industry.
We look forward to working closely with BTEA and EWB to create new opportunities for engagement, knowledge exchange and collaboration across our community.
ANDREW: What surprised you about the event?
CHRIS: UFI events always surprise and delight me. It is always a pleasure to see the engagement between delegates, sponsors, speakers and our hosts, and this year it was as valuable as ever.
If I had to pick one thing, it would be the Gala Dinner. The setting, the food and the entertainment were incredible, and I certainly did not expect to hold a falcon.
UFI will work closely with BTEA and EWB to create new opportunities for engagement, knowledge exchange and collaboration across the events community.
ANDREW: Can you share some details about this year’s Medal of Honour winners?
CHRIS: The UFI Medal of Honour recognizes exceptional, long-term contributions to our industry and the UFI community.
This year, it went to three remarkable people. Paul Woodward has devoted decades to the exhibition industry and to UFI, including as UFI Managing Director from 2010-2015.
Ray Bloom, Chairman of IMEX Group, is a true community builder who has connected our global business events community.
Ravinder Sethi, Executive Chairman of R.E. Rogers India, has long been a passionate UFI ambassador across India and the Asia-Pacific region.
ANDREW: How can young or emerging professionals get involved with UFI?
CHRIS: There are several ways. They can apply to our Next Generation Leadership Programme, attend UFI events, ask to take part in our Working Groups and explore the Exhibition Essentials program.
They can also encourage their organization to enter the UFI Awards, which are a great way to showcase the work of their team.
ANDREW: What do you expect for the events industry in 2027 — and how can young or emerging professionals prepare for success?
CHRIS: In 2027, I hope we continue to make progress on how we measure success.

For too long, our industry has relied on square meters sold. Organizers, exhibitors and visitors increasingly need measures that matter to them, such as the number and quality of leads, meetings and business generated, and the tools to track them.

I also expect AI to keep moving from experimentation to practical use, delivering better experiences, smoother processes and leaner operations. Smart matchmaking can even help large events feel smaller by ensuring the right buyers and sellers find each other. But the core value of our industry will not change: Technology should support face-to-face connection, not replace it.
For young professionals, my advice is simple: Get involved. A great first step is to attend a UFI regional event, and there is one in every region over the next nine months.
